firstofitskind south dakota cohousing development finds its place in vermillion in this college town of 11000 a handful of longtime residents are building the states firstever cohousing development which they hope provides a new way of living for them and frees up traditional homes for others cohousing doesnt just create houses it creates a community and it does that very intentionally said betty smith a founding member of the group cohousing is a method of living that prioritizes community connection and growth residents live in small houses with a large common house as the centerpiece where community events and regular shared meals are a cornerstone of the living style common houses usually contain large kitchens dining and living rooms and are central gathering places for the residents at the vermillion development called dakota prairie commons there will also be an emphasis on walkability with footpaths connecting houses the campus itself will be vehiclefree parking and garages will sit at the periphery of the development smith said and while residents will have their own homes they will be encouraged to rely on others for many daytoday activities one of my favorite stories is going to iowa citys cohousing and walking in and i compliment this womans dog i said oh what a wonderful dog and she says oh thats not my dog thats my neighbors dog im taking care of it this week and then somebody else says oh and i have the dog next week im so excited its that easy but its also significant things like if somebody breaks an arm you know youve got closeby neighbors smith said the concept also helps to combat isolation and loneliness as residents get to know their neighbors and begin to feel like part of the community smith said isolation and depression is a national thing right now its a huge health issue smith said and this really responds to those needs everybody knows everyone else and is willing to be part of the community and support one another thats huge response years of planning equals placemaking smith a former professor at the university of south dakota taught classes on city planning and zoning which is how she came across the concept of cohousing it has been more than a decade since she first started to consider the idea as a viable living solution in vermillion now after years of planning the group has officially found both its land and a developer to work on it the site is comprised of 5 acres of a total 15acre plot purchased by ams building systems just east of downtown vermillion it will eventually feature 28 homes which will open in stages over the next few years smith said ten equity members have already put up a financial stake and are confirmed to move into the development when it opens other members which the group calls explorers have made small financial commitments to have access to planning and other community information as they decide whether cohousing is right for them besides providing a new type of living for its residents dakota prairie commons will help ease vermillions housing crunch by adding freedup homes to the market one real estate broker has already offered discounts on brokerage fees to those moving into cohousing and looking to sell their house in the vermillion area smith said one of the advantages of building something like this in a town like vermillion is theres a real housing shortage here a 2022 housing study showed that we are missing housing for people who work here for faculty at usd for senior citizens there are a lot of gaps in housing and its really hard to attract developers who will develop out this way smith said new faculty members come and often wait two years before a house comes on the market for them well were all going to be selling our houses evidence interest in vermillion and from elsewhere while many of the future residents are older the community is decidedly not a senior citizens complex a discussion that was brought on when a younger professor at usd said they were interested in moving in smith said the project is also drawing outside interest someone who currently lives in north carolina plans to move to vermillion when the development is completed she said one of the things i didnt realize when smith first started talking to me about this is we would not need to find 28 households of people from vermillion becky rider another equity member told news watch people will move from other parts of the country to where theres cohousing because the community to them is more important than exactly where its located the vermillion community as a whole has also embraced the concept smith said the group recently hosted an open house event where city residents had the chance to ask questions about cohousing and the development itself which smith said was wellattended phd students studying sustainability at usd have also offered to do research on the site assisting with native grass design composting and recycling systems smith said its cool that nobodys done this yet in the area theyre still trying to wrap their head around what cohousing really is but they have a much better idea after listening to all of us going through the process she said insights ongoing conversations create collaborative environment members of the cohousing group met recently to discuss what features were most important to them via smallcircle conversations and brainstorming sessions that collaboration is one of the key features of cohousing that makes it different from traditional development smith said during those discussions there were themes that emerged that were very different from the traditional cohousing path especially considering that many existing cohousing communities are located in much more temperate coastal towns far from south dakotas subzero winters we like to say were doing it the vermillion way smith said were not following a strictly cohousing path as many of the longtime communities on the coasts have were branching out and doing it our way priorities of future residents were varied but had specific focus on elements that involved people coming together fire pits community gardens outdoor classrooms diane leja an equity member of dakota prairie commons said she envisions a space in the common house where residents can share items that are useful but only needed occasionally so members rely on each other more and consider themselves part of the community the concept of shared goods is especially important when considering that dakota prairie commons hopes to focus on sustainability said susanne skyrm another equity member its so much more sustainable than everybody having a great big house and a great big yard building these days is not always done with efficiency in mind thats definitely one of our prerogatives is building it so it is sustainable skyrm said everybody doesnt need their own turkey roaster you can have one in the common house and everybody else can use it youre sharing things and not having everybody buying something they only use once a year limitations some higher costs require a reminder of rewards the housing model allows for greater community building better connections with neighbors and extra support when its needed so why has it not caught on more across the country well its a lot of work rider said and we are the ones that have been doing the work over the years i mean this is years in the making already its much different than just building a regular neighborhood and in some cases residents may have to make some financial tradeoffs to join cohousing communities especially in the early stages by the time you pay for land and a portion of the common house and your own house its not inexpensive we live in a house that would be a good starter house for somebody when we move out but its going to very likely cost us more to move into the cohousing rider said so while were trying to keep it affordable were not thinking of subsidizing our building costs or anything its affordable with a small a right now but the payoff especially for these longtime vermillion residents some of whom have been in the community for decades will be worth it leja said i think in some ways were going back to older models its a throwback in a lot of ways your neighbors you used to do things together i mean we grew up having block parties and barbecues with our neighbors on our street and that doesnt happen very much anymore leja said

welcome to the confident nurse community whether youre in nursing school brandnew to the floor or years into your career you belong here this is a space for anyone who wants to grow in confidence share lessons and connect with others who get it being a confident nurse isnt about knowing everything its about presence its walking into a room and knowing your voice matters its building trust with patients and coworkers its supporting one another through wins struggles and the lessons that shape us and just as important this community shines a light on the real issues in nursing and healthcare things that often go unnoticed or unspoken here we can talk about them openly honestly and respectfully so we learn and grow together what this space is for weekly tips and lessons to build your confidence honest stories from nursing school to the icu and everywhere in between support for new grads students and seasoned nurses alike thoughtful respectful conversations about the challenges in our profession this isnt just another forum its a community jump in introduce yourself in the comments your name or nickname where you are in your journey student new grad nurse exploring one tip lesson or story thats shaped your confidence drop it below we cant wait to hear from you

navigating a reevaluation in wants and needs in a relationship looking for some perspective thoughts and experiences from others regarding a specific process im in with my partner we have been together for over a year hes younger than me and our life situations differ hes still in a life stage where he needs to do all the exploring and figuring himself out and i have done a lot of that in the past few years and am currently building a stable life for myself i didnt realise until a recent discussion we had that i had been unconsciously placing him in a spot in my life where he would be a part of that stabilizing and settling which he communicated that hes not ready to make long term plans with me since he doesnt even know yet what kind of a life he wants to lead and im happy to support him in the exploration i just took an emotional hit of expectations crumbled that i didnt even fully realise i had but this discussion did make me realise that i am looking to settle and make long term plans with someone and i have felt quite emotional about the fact that its a need i have which i havent given myself the space or permission to actually pursue so currently im having a mix of many emotions that are hard for me to separate which is the grief over my own selfabandonment and which is the disappointment of building castles in my head over one relationship that cant fulfill those dreams and i wish i could focus on building our relationship with more clarity of what we both are looking for but the blurring of my different emotions is just making the situation a bit hard for me to navigate currently i guess the issue is that theres no representation for situations where these discussions dont end up in break ups and id love to hear experiences and thoughts from other poly folk who possibly have faced something similar

how to quit smoking without losing your mind what actually works according to science you know whats wild we all know smoking kills its literally on the package but quitting feels impossible and most people fail multiple times before it sticks ive spent months researching this from every angle books medical journals podcasts with addiction specialists youtube deep dives because honestly the way we talk about smoking cessation is broken we treat it like a willpower problem when its actually a neuroscience problem nicotine rewires your brains reward system it hijacks the same pathways that make you enjoy food sex and connection your brain literally thinks it needs cigarettes to survive so when people fail to quit its not weakness its biology fighting against you but heres the thing once you understand how this works you can actually use it to your advantage the actual science of why quitting sucks your brain on nicotine is basically a hostage situation every cigarette floods your brain with dopamine after a few weeks of smoking your brain reduces its natural dopamine production because it expects the cigarettes to do the job this is why that first cigarette of the day feels incredible and why going without feels like actual physical pain the withdrawal timeline is predictable but brutal physical withdrawal peaks around 72 hours thats when most people crack but the psychological cravings can last months understanding this timeline helps because you know whats coming instead of thinking something is wrong with you atomic habits by james clear changed how i think about this completely clear is a habits expert whos sold over 15 million copies because his approach actually works he breaks down the neuroscience of habit loops cue craving response reward smoking isnt one habit its dozens morning coffee cigarette post meal cigarette stress cigarette you need to identify every single trigger and create a replacement behavior for each one insanely practical read that makes behavior change feel manageable instead of overwhelming the book explains something crucial you cant just remove a bad habit you have to replace it so if you smoke when stressed you need a new stress response ready to go deep breathing a quick walk literally anything that interrupts the pattern strategies that actually move the needle nicotine replacement therapy isnt cheating patches gum lozenges they double your success rate the goal isnt to white knuckle through withdrawal its to separate the nicotine addiction from the behavioral addiction once you break the ritual of smoking tapering off nicotine is way easier theres a prescription medication called varenicline chantix that blocks nicotine receptors in your brain it makes smoking less satisfying and reduces cravings success rates are significantly higher than going cold turkey talk to your doctor about whether it makes sense for you some people get vivid dreams or mood changes as side effects but for many its a game changer the app smoke free tracks your progress in real time money saved health improvements craving patterns it gamifies quitting in a way that actually helps you can log cravings and it shows you they get shorter and less intense over time seeing the data makes the invisible visible if you want something more structured that pulls from multiple addiction experts and research theres an app called befreed that creates personalized learning plans for quitting based on your specific triggers and patterns built by a team from columbia and google it turns content from books like the easy way to stop smoking research on addiction neuroscience and expert talks into customized audio sessions you tell it your goal like quit smoking as someone who uses it for stress relief and it builds a plan just for you the depth is adjustable too from quick 10minute sessions to 40minute deep dives when you need more strategies and examples its been helpful for understanding the psychology behind my smoking patterns without needing to read multiple books cover to cover cognitive behavioral therapy techniques work incredibly well for smoking the easy way to stop smoking by allen carr has helped millions of people quit carr was a chain smoker who eventually founded clinics worldwide his approach is controversial because he claims you dont need willpower at all instead he dismantles the psychological dependence by reframing how you think about cigarettes you stop seeing them as a pleasure youre giving up and start seeing them as a parasite youre evicting this is the best smoking cessation book ive ever read the mindset shift is powerful urge surfing is a technique where you ride out cravings like waves instead of fighting them cravings peak at around 35 minutes then fade if you can distract yourself for that window call someone do pushups play a phone game the urge passes the more you practice this the weaker future cravings become identify your smoking triggers ruthlessly keep a journal for a few days before you quit when do you smoke what emotions precede it who are you with once you know your patterns you can disrupt them if you always smoke with morning coffee switch to tea for a month if you smoke after meals immediately brush your teeth instead make it impossible to run on autopilot the brutal truth about relapse most people need multiple attempts to quit permanently the average person tries 7 times before it sticks this isnt failure its data collection what triggered the relapse what will you do differently next time one cigarette is not the end the fuck it mentality after a slip up causes more damage than the cigarette itself if you slip dont buy a pack dont decide youve failed literally just dont smoke the next cigarette the app i am sober isnt just for alcohol it works great for smoking too you can connect with others quitting track your sober time and get daily motivational content the community aspect helps because you realize youre not alone in this fight social and environmental hacks tell everyone youre quitting social accountability works ask friends not to offer you cigarettes avoid smokers for the first few weeks if possible it sounds harsh but your health matters more than social comfort change your environment aggressively wash everything that smells like smoke get your car detailed throw out lighters and ashtrays eliminate every cue you can find a quit buddy success rates jump when you quit with someone else you can text each other when cravings hit dopamine nation by dr anna lembke explores addiction and recovery in the modern world lembke is a stanford psychiatrist and addiction medicine specialist the book explains how our brains adapt to constant dopamine stimulation and why abstinence can actually reset your reward system she talks about the dopamine deficit state that happens after you quit anything addictive smoking social media whatever your brain needs time to recalibrate understanding this helped me realize the misery is temporary and necessary the timeline of getting better 72 hours in nicotine is out of your system withdrawal peaks you feel awful but youre through how to be hot and smart without being cringe the psychology behind it okay so ive been noticing this weird thing where people either lean super hard into being the hot one or the smart one like theyre mutually exclusive brands its bizarre like you have to pick a lane and stick with it or risk coming off as fake ive spent way too much time studying this books podcasts random psychology rabbit holes on youtube because i was tired of watching genuinely cool people dim themselves down to fit some imaginary box the truth is society kind of sets us up for this were conditioned to believe intelligence threatens attractiveness and vice versa but thats complete bullshit the real issue isnt being both its the performative energy people bring when they try to be both thats what makes it cringe heres what actually works stop performing and start integrating the tryhard vibe comes from treating intelligence and attractiveness like accessories you put on for different occasions youre not method acting two different characters psychologist carl rogers talked about congruence basically when your internal self matches your external presentation thats the secret sauce when youre genuinely comfortable being smart and caring about how you look it stops feeling like a performance people can smell incongruence from a mile away physical attractiveness is just basic maintenance not a personality heres the thing nobody wants to hear taking care of yourself physically isnt some massive achievement worth broadcasting its baseline adulting you dont need to post gym selfies with captions about grinding or make your entire personality i read philosophy just do both quietly mark mansons book the subtle art of not giving a fck dudes a nyt bestselling author and his writing is insanely practical breaks this down perfectly he argues that trying to prove your worth through external markers is exactly what makes you less attractive the paradox is real stop announcing it and just be it curiosity beats performance every time actual intelligence isnt about flexing your vocab or name dropping philosophers you read once its about being genuinely curious ask better questions listen like you actually care i started using this app called waking up sam harriss meditation app and one of the practices is literally just paying full attention to conversations without planning your response sounds simple but its wild how rare that is when youre present and curious rather than waiting to showcase how smart you are people actually want to be around you attractiveness is 80 energy anyway read books that make you more human not more pretentious theres a difference between reading to genuinely expand your worldview versus reading so you can mention it at parties sapiens by yuval noah harari this book sold over 20 million copies and the guys a historian at hebrew university completely changed how i think about human behavior and society but heres what makes it actually useful it doesnt make you sound smarter in conversations it makes you more curious and humble because you realize how much you dont know thats the vibe you want same with thinking fast and slow by daniel kahneman nobel prize winner in economics itll make you question literally every assumption you have about how your brain works for people who dont have time to read full books but still want the knowledge theres befreed a personalized learning app built by columbia alumni and ai experts you type in what you want to work on like become more magnetic while staying intellectually curious and it pulls from psychology research books like the ones mentioned above and expert insights to create custom audio content whats useful is you can adjust the depth from a quick 10minute overview to a 40minute deep dive with actual examples and context the voice options are weirdly addictive too theres this smoky sarcastic tone that makes dense material way more listenable during commutes or at the gym it also builds you a structured learning plan that evolves as you use it so its not just random content but a real path toward who you want to become develop taste not a persona hot and smart people have taste they know what they like and why theyre not following some aesthetic algorithm or trying to optimize their personality for maximum appeal they just have opinions that come from actual exploration start a letterboxd and actually watch films beyond marvel movies use an app like ash relationship and mental health coach to understand your patterns better listen to podcasts like huberman lab where andrew huberman stanford neuroscientist breaks down actual science in ways that are accessible but not dumbed down the point isnt to become some cultured intellectual its to feed your brain interesting inputs so you naturally have interesting outputs your body language matters more than your resume ive noticed people obsess over credentials and appearance details while completely ignoring how they carry themselves slouched shoulders avoiding eye contact fidgeting nervously that tanks attractiveness faster than any physical feature amy cuddys research on power poses yeah there was some controversy about replication but the core idea holds shows how your physical posture literally changes your hormones and confidence levels stand up straight make eye contact move through space like you belong there not arrogant just present stop seeking validation for being both the most cringe thing is fishing for compliments about being the whole package or whatever if you need external validation that youre hot and smart youre still performing the goal is internal congruence where youre genuinely comfortable being multidimensional most people are interesting when you actually get to know them they just hide it because theyre scared of being too much be too much the right people will stay embrace being a walking contradiction you can deadlift heavy and cry during pixar movies you can read dense philosophy and watch trashy reality tv you can care about skincare and particle physics the cringe comes from pretending youre one dimensional because you think thats more believable glennon doyle talks about this in untamed was on nyt bestseller list forever and shes incredible at dismantling social expectations she basically says we spend our whole lives trying to be palatable when were most magnetic as our full complicated selves look nobodys keeping score except you stop trying to prove youre hot stop trying to prove youre smart just be someone who takes care of themselves and feeds their mind because it feels good not because it looks good thats literally the entire secret everything else is just noise

the apartment above yours final part you finally turn around there is no one standing behind you your bedroom door is open but the hallway beyond it is wrong too long too dark like it stretches farther than your apartment should allow behind you the ceiling groans not creaks groans like something alive is pressing against it from the other side the wet stain above your bed spreads outward in veins drops begin falling faster nowthick sticky warm when one lands on your hand you realize it isnt water its saliva a voice comes from inside the ceiling muffled panicked overlapping itself like multiple mouths speaking through one throat i cant breathe right anymore the ceiling bulges downward violently you hear bones cracking not yours something punches through not breaking the concretesliding through it like the ceiling has turned soft a hand drops into your room then another then a head forces itself out face stretched sideways jaw unhinged eyes bulging and unfocused like it forgot how to see its mouth opens wide and black liquid pours out splashing onto your bed the smell hits you fully now hospital disinfectant old blood rot you scream the thing in the ceiling screams backbut louder and deeper and wrong like its lungs are filled with something else then you hear footsteps above you running multiple sets the ceiling begins to open not crackingpeeling like skin being pulled apart arms fall out legs bodies they drop into your room one by one slamming onto the floor in broken piles their limbs are bent backward torsos twisted flat faces permanently pressed sideways like theyve spent years crushed between floors they twitch they inhale sharply in unison one of them turns its head toward you with a wet snapping sound its mouth moves too slow for the words that come out youre in our ceiling your vision tunnels your ears ring your phone vibrates in your pocket a notification lights the screen building management rooftop access scheduled 213 am the lights go out complete darkness you feel hands touching your legs your arms your ribs cold wet exploring something climbs onto your bed something presses down on your chest its weight feels wrongtoo spread out like a body flattened thin a mouth presses against your ear it whispers they said if someone moved in we could come down your bedroom ceiling collapses inward with a deafening crack and as concrete bodies and darkness fall onto you the last thing you hear is the building settling like it finally has enough space

article fallout 76 leads plan to make the game thicker with new systems as the team cant just continue making the map bigger and bigger just read this article where they interviewed the devs and theres some interesting things in there ive included the most interesting bits below for those who dont want to click the link speaking to pcgamesn creative director jon rush and lead producer bill lacoste explained that the goal is to make fallout 76 thicker with new systems that encourage experimentation earlier this year when we sat down with the two they explained that there are years of updates already cooking but it seems that the plan is to also make existing content deeper with retrofitted systems we have had a couple of successful literal expansions of the map you know making the play space bigger rush said for this next year i really want our gaze to shift from the outskirts to inwards make the game thicker new systems or new ways to engage with existing content those are all very much on the menu for this year while the team has spent years bolstering the size of the game world over the years rush explains that they cant only do that while they would love to continue exploring areas outside of the current map they explained there are technical considerations that have to be taken into account there so we cant just continue making the map bigger and bigger its worth noting that fallout 76 is built on an older forked version of fallout 4s creation engine not the newer creation engine 2 there are some builtin limitations such as the lack of crossplay or crosssave features but the team does explain that there is still a lot of the map still left to explore in future expansions there is a lot of space left on the existing map in the game that is unused that maybe down the road we could open up if it supports the stories that we want to tell and if we think players would have a fun time exploring those regions and building there and whatnot rush continued

what if aging didnt mean shrinking your world but growing a village ive been thinking a lot about how weird it is that we treat aging like a solo sport you work your whole life you raise kids build things fix things survive things and then society basically says congrats now go sit quietly and dont be in the way that feels wrong what if instead of drifting apart healthy or relatively healthy seniors came together to share skills cooking gardening repairs finances art caregiving life wisdom live near or with people who get what aging actually feels like support each other before we need institutions create kinship that isnt based only on blood pass knowledge forward instead of letting it disappear not a retirement home not a cult not a commune with rules and uniforms more like a chosen family of elders who still want to participate in life not just observe it imagine someone teaches you how to can tomatoes someone helps you fix a door someone sits with you when your arthritis flares up someone remembers how to make soup when money was tight someone listens because theyve also lost people this isnt about being forever young its about being useful connected and human for as long as possible im curious would you want to be part of something like this what would you want to contribute what would make it feel safe not creepy if enough people are interested id love to start a small online space just to explore the idea together not a business pitch not a survey just a conversation about how we want to age because maybe the future of aging isnt isolation maybe its kinship

i have written my college essay for uw art major thoughts okay its time to line up everybody i looked both ways before slipping my book into my raggedy backpack okay fourthgrade class its time to check out your books i added my books to the tan counter and looked up at the older woman checking them out we referred to her as chicken legs she was topheavy yet had thin muscular legs that resembled well a chicken this it she asked oh gosh what am i doing yes i declared next i walked on i didnt dare open my bag or pull out the book for the rest of the day patiently waiting until i got home i was a thief but a patient thief i finally reached the confines of my room it had gray concrete floors and ugly wood paneling that the rest of our house also proudly sported i took my backpack accomplice off and set it on my bed i ran into my parents room into their spooky closet and stole sheets of paper we may have had to wait for tax returns to get new toothbrushes but we always had a surplus of art supplies i bolted back to my room i opened my bag and pulled out my valuable stolen artifact draw 50 famous cartoons by lee j ames it was brown and worn a book that did not belong in 2013 but somewhere in the 80s i drew every cartoon from that book carefully attempting to mimic the cartoons my favorite being felix the cat i showed my mom and she proudly hung it on the fridge and that is where my love for art began art became my escape i would paint my thoughts and feelings and then hide them in my closet when angry i would paint my mom and dad as ugly disfigured trolls when finished i would walk to the bathroom and run water over the paper until it became a gross squishy lump then i would rip apart the mush and throw it in the trash where my crime could not be discovered this thanks

poor experience with dr j colleagues adhd assessment right to choose im turning 30 this year and have long suspected i have adhd i finally put the pieces together properly in summer 2025 my partner had noticed i was having a particularly rough patch with adhd symptoms and my sister whod been diagnosed the previous year and found medication lifechanging had also suggested i might want to look into an assessment after speaking with friends whod been through the process i approached my gp in august 2025 my gp was great and signposted me to right to choose listing five clinics to choose from dr j colleagues had one of the shorter wait times not the shortest but reasonable and decent reviews so i went with them i submitted my referral on 6 august and heard absolutely nothing from dr j colleagues until 22 october when they finally acknowledged it they appointment date came through two days later then on 3 november they sent through their poorly formatted forms in mixed file types asking me to complete them within a week before my appointment on 10 november they were a nightmare to complete but i did them thoroughly with years of school reports input from my parents the lot the appointment was scheduled for an hour with a nurse practitioner she spent the first 20 minutes asking fairly robotic questions about basic details that were already in my forms i didnt feel she was particularly interested in exploring my symptoms in depth then about 15 minutes in she revealed she hadnt been able to access any of my forms the admin team had uploaded them as a zip file which apparently she couldnt open so wed need to reschedule she rebooked for two days later but only for 30 minutes this time on the second call she joined without her camera on and told me straight away id met the criteria for inattentive adhd based on the forms and that id get a report in eight weeks and titration within three months but no additional questions or exploration of symptoms and the call was concluded within about five minutes so now i have an adhd diagnosis but very little confidence in whether i actually have it or just met the right criteria on my forms id expected much more interrogation of what id written and what else could be going on the report arrived eight weeks later and was very detailed but mostly just repeating back what id put in the forms my medication appointment was scheduled for 12 weeks after diagnosis i shuffled other commitments around to make space for it and started mentally preparing to begin medication a week before the appointment they asked for health information i sent it heard no acknowledgement then got a generic email asking for it again one day before the appointment i got another template email saying it had been cancelled due to unforeseen business and clinical demands to prioritise patients already on titration the waiting list is now apparently four months long and my wait has been extended by about a month no new session scheduled yet im beyond disappointed i know im probably on a fairly typical timeline and that these clinics are under massive pressure but the whole experience has been shoddy the communication is appalling the forms could be sorted overnight if someone could be spent half an hour updating them and the assessment itself felt worryingly superficial hopefully theyll schedule the medication appointment soon but im left feeling like my diagnosis isnt particularly secure

what is your unique attraction to the game of chess what is your attraction to chess chess is a world unto itselfa microcosm of human thought creativity and interaction condensed onto sixtyfour squares for some it is a battlefield for others a canvas and for many a sanctuary of endless fascination its appeal is as varied as the minds it captivates drawing people into its depths in ways that go far beyond the simple act of moving pawns and knights ones attraction to chess can manifest in playing spectating teaching writing designing analyzing or simply delighting in the sheer elegance of its patterns in short chess is not just a gameit is a multidimensional experience a mirror reflecting both intellect and imagination at the most obvious level chess attracts people through play the thrill of a carefully calculated attack the subtle tension of a positional squeeze or the exhilaration of a clever tactical combination is addictive every game is a story unfolding in real time with openings as introductions middlegames as intricate plots and endgames as dramatic climaxes the joy of winning of outsmarting an opponent through foresight and strategy is powerfulbut for many the process itself the mental dance of possibilities is just as compelling players often describe a sense of flow a state in which time seems suspended as their minds navigate branching sequences of potential moves each with its own consequences chess transforms abstract thinking into a tangible experience of strategy and foresight creating a unique form of intellectual excitement yet the attraction extends far beyond the act of playing spectating chess has its own allure watching grandmasters duel in international tournaments can be as mesmerizing as a symphony or theater performance enthusiasts revel in brilliant sacrifices dramatic blunders and timepressure scrambles following the silent conversation between minds across the board for some observing games is a form of meditationa way to study strategy absorb creativity and witness the beauty of ideas unfolding without the pressure of participation in this sense chess captivates not only those who move the pieces but also those who appreciate the elegance of thought itself chess also inspires creative expression and intellectual exploration writers and journalists have long been drawn to the game producing novels essays and commentaries that explore its history psychology and drama artists find inspiration in chess boards and pieces using them in sculptures paintings or graphic designs where the blackandwhite geometry becomes a motif for balance conflict and harmony even chess puzzlesseemingly simple arrangements of piecescan become works of art blending logic aesthetics and ingenuity this marriage of creativity and intellect makes chess alluring to those who delight in thinking deeply and imagining boldly mathematics and geometry offer yet another avenue of attraction chess is a playground of patterns probabilities and spatial reasoning each piece moves in distinctive geometric pathways the knights lshaped leaps the bishops diagonals and the rooks straight lines players and theorists often marvel at the combinatorial explosion of possibilitiesevery move opening countless branches of potential futures for minds attuned to logic chess offers an inexhaustible source of problems sequences and structures to analyze dissect and master here fascination is fueled not by competition but by the intellectual beauty of order symmetry and complexity chess also thrives in the social and educational spheres teaching and mentoring offer profound rewards as experienced players guide novices through openings tactics and endgames passing on not only skills but also values patience concentration resilience and critical thinking street chess and local clubs transform the game into a social ritual where conversations rivalries and camaraderie coexist with strategy in these spaces chess becomes a bridge between generations cultures and communities offering connection and shared joy beyond the abstract intellectual challenge even the love of chess itselfthe pure almost instinctive fascination with its infinite possibilitiesdraws people in some are captivated by the historical narratives of legendary matches others by the drama of a sudden checkmate and yet others by the quiet satisfaction of seeing a plan unfold successfully chess offers a sense of mastery discovery and beauty that is deeply personal yet universally accessible its appeal is not limited to traditional play it is found in writing about chess analyzing games designing artistic boards exploring mathematical structures and mentoring the next generation of players ultimately the attraction to chess is multifaceted and deeply human it appeals to our intellect imagination creativity and social instincts simultaneously whether one plays watches writes teaches or dreams about the game chess offers a universe of possibilitieseach as rich challenging and beautiful as the next it is a game a science an art form and a social fabric all in one its power lies not only in the moves themselves but in the endless ways people engage with them reflecting the complexity curiosity and passion that define human thought in chess there is always something new to explore a fresh challenge to meet and a subtle beauty to appreciate the games allure is timeless universal and uniquely personala mirror of both the mind and the spirit

welcome to rhynoteapp the official hynote community this subreddit is a space for people who are experimenting with or curious about using ai to capture notes meetings and ideas without being glued to a keyboard a lot of us are here for the same reason taking notes by hand or typing nonstop pulls attention away from the actual conversation whether its meetings lectures brainstorming sessions or quick voice thoughts the goal is to stay present and still walk away with something useful this community isnt just about features or updates its about realworld use what actually works in meetings and what doesnt how accurate ai summaries feel over time privacy concerns and how people handle them inperson vs virtual setups apple watch phone workflows when ai helps and when it gets in the way if youre using hynote already feel free to share your experiences honestly good bad or confusing if youre just exploring ai notetaking in general youre welcome too comparisons alternatives and workflows are all fair game no strict rules here just keep it respectful and useful ask questions share experiments and talk about what you wish these tools did better looking forward to hearing how people are actually using ai to think more not type more

theory silver wolf follows the path of elation now that we know our favorite cute hacker will be getting a new playable character in the upcoming versions set in planarcadia i thought it would be a good time to revisit some of the most overlooked parts of silver wolfs writing to shed light on lore bits i suspect a large portion of the playerbase still ignores to this day the purpose of this post is to draw parallels between sw and some of the currently known masked fools while there is no actual evidence of her being a follower of the path of elation it would at least explain some coincidences perhaps sw was an elation pathstrider in the past or maybe her character was initially written to be a masked fool before she was given a larger role to play in the story as a stellaron hunter instead if she jokes like a fool in case you didnt notice silver wolf often breaks the fourth wall one of the best examples of this is a message players can receive after pulling her where she sends us a screenshot of her ingame achievement menu this to me is undeniable proof that sw has some degree of awareness of honkai star rail as a video game you know who else likes to break the fourth wall all the time elation pathstriders the masked fools tell a parable of the birth of their beloved aeon when the aeon of elation climbed to the highest branch on the tree of existence they saw the cold and despicable void the stars operating like machinery and how the meaning of all things bows before nothingness the fools believe that the truth of the world is a joke and that the ultimate meaning of all things lies in mere laughter the masked fools are a group of selfaware characters just like the aeon they follow sampo speaks to the player towards the end of the in the sweltering morning sun quest and hanabi does the same in the myriad celestia trailer sparkle behind the curtain video even ahas sim in the simulated universe managed to realize that theyre nothing but a character in a simulation speaking of the simulated universe the elation blessings are full of pop culture references lives like a fool on a superficial level silver wolf has always kept a very happygolucky attitude in every piece of media she has appeared in so far shes always eager to play new games with us and the fact she keeps on losing doesnt seem to bother her much you know who else likes to live just to have fun all the time elation pathstriders wealth status power none of those matters to sparkle the only thing that can get her attention is amusement and games with a fool after farewell penacony hanabi reveals to us in a message that she was hired by a friend she made while gaming the dialogue implies that this person is silver wolf as hanabi talks about a gamer with a script just like the script elio gives to the stellaron hunters this was later confirmed by hanabi herself silver wolf never mentioned me but shes the one who invited me to team up how did sw get the privilege to game with hanabi we know nothing about their relationship isnt it a bit too convenient for them to know each other of course elios foreseeing powers could explain why and how sw got in contact with hanabi but i wonder if their relationship will be explored further in planarcadia then is she a fool there is no real evidence to suggest silver wolf is or used to be a masked fool quite the contrary one might argue that sw doesnt have a mask however neither does sampo and yet he was still considered a member of the masked fools even after being separated from his mask but then again doesnt sw wear something that could be considered a mask of sorts im talking about her goggles both the ones sw wears and the messengers holovisor from the relic set messenger traversing hackerspace can be considered masks in a broader sense speaking of sampo our best buddy and sw share a similar distrust of the masked fools as a whole since you can never know for sure what a fool is really up to you never know what kind of crazy stunt a masked fool follower of the elation might pull for the sake of having fun look when youre dealing with someone wearing a mask you gotta keep your wits about you in our group there are some who cant read the room i just dont like communicating with people like that its so dull everyone has their own way of pursuing elation why must i waste my own energy sharing my sense of aesthetics with others heh a joke with too heavy a tone can bring trouble as this trouble builds what was once funny becomes no longer fun sw and sampo have their own distinct ways of having fun separate from other elation pathstriders but so do hanabi and giovanni is it really so farfetched to think they all tread the same path

stop explaining your boundaries the psychology that actually works real talk youve probably spent years justifying why you cant work late defending why you need alone time apologizing for saying no meanwhile your boundaries are still getting trampled because heres what nobody tells you the more you explain the weaker your boundary becomes i spent months reading everything i could find on this psychology papers behavioral research podcasts from therapists bren browns work on vulnerability nedra glover tawwabs boundary breakdowns and the pattern was clear people who hold strong boundaries dont negotiate them they just enforce them period this isnt about becoming some cold unfeeling robot its about understanding that boundaries are not debate topics theyre decisions youve made about how you want to live and when you treat them like they need a powerpoint presentation to be valid youre basically telling people theyre optional step 1 understand why youre over explaining your boundary isnt the problem your need to justify it is and that need usually comes from guilt programming youve been taught that saying no without a good enough reason makes you selfish spoiler alert it doesnt fear of conflict you think if you explain hard enough people will understand and magically respect your limits they wont people respect boundaries when there are consequences not because your reasoning was persuasive enough people pleasing tendencies youd rather exhaust yourself explaining than deal with someone being upset with you for five minutes seeking validation deep down youre asking permission for your own boundaries youre waiting for someone to say okay that reason is acceptable but heres the thing you dont need anyones approval research from the journal of personality and social psychology shows that people with weaker boundaries actually experience more relationship conflict not less all that explaining isnt keeping the peace its inviting negotiation step 2 stop using jadeing therapists have a term for what youre doing jade justify argue defend explain every time you jade youre opening a door for someone to push back i cant come to dinner because i have to wake up early for a meeting and ive been really tired lately and my doctor said i need more sleep and see what happened there you gave them five different angles to attack just have one drink you can sleep in the car skip the morning meeting compare that to i cant make it tonight no explanation no wiggle room no negotiation just a clear calm statement this feels brutal at first your brain will scream at you that youre being rude youre not youre just not performing emotional labor to make someone else comfortable with your decision step 3 practice the power of that doesnt work for me this phrase is magic its firm but not aggressive it gives zero information for someone to argue against can you cover my shift that doesnt work for me why not heres where most people crack and start explaining dont just repeat it doesnt work for me if they keep pushing you can add im not able to do that notice youre still not giving reasons youre just restating the boundary in different words dr henry clouds book boundaries seriously read this one its insanely good and has helped millions of people reclaim their lives breaks down how boundaries are about taking responsibility for your own choices not managing other peoples reactions the book won multiple christian book awards but the principles apply to anyone clouds background as a clinical psychologist shows in every page this is the best boundary book out there hands down step 4 get comfortable with awkward silence after you state your boundary without explaining theres usually this heavy silence the other person is waiting for you to fill it with justifications dont let it sit let them process let them be uncomfortable with your no this is where boundaries are won or lost if you can sit in that tension without caving youve just shown them your boundary is real most people cave in the silence thats why their boundaries dont stick silence isnt rude its just space and in that space the other person has to decide if theyre going to respect your boundary or not but either way youre not negotiating step 5 remove yourself when boundaries are violated words mean nothing without action if someone crosses your boundary after youve stated it leave the conversation hang up walk away end the email thread ive said im not discussing this and then you stay in the discussion your boundary just became a suggestion physical removal is the most powerful enforcement tool you have its not dramatic its not mean its just following through if you want to go deeper on boundary psychology but struggle to find time for dense books or dont know where to start with all the research befreed is a personalized learning app that pulls from psychology books research papers and expert interviews to create custom audio content tailored to your goals type something specific like im a people pleaser who struggles to set boundaries without feeling guilty and it generates a structured learning plan with episodes ranging from quick 10 minute summaries to 40 minute deep dives with real examples the content adapts based on what you highlight and how you interact with your virtual coach plus you can customize the voice even choosing that smoky confident tone that makes the tough psychology lessons easier to absorb during your commute or workout step 6 stop apologizing for existing sorry but i cant take on more work right now sorry for bothering you but could you keep the noise down sorry i need to cancel why are you apologizing youre not sorry youre just uncomfortable that someone might be disappointed but their disappointment is not your emergency cut the sorry unless youve actually done something wrong replace it with nothing or with thanks for understanding tara brachs work on radical acceptance check out her podcast tara brach on insight timer its free and her talks on self compassion are game changing explores how we apologize for our needs because weve internalized the message that our needs are burdensome theyre not theyre just needs step 7 practice with low stakes situations dont start enforcing boundaries with your overbearing mother or toxic boss start small practice with strangers cashiers customer service would you like to donate to no thank you no explanation about your budget or other charities you support just a clean no can i get your email for promotions no thanks these micro practices build the muscle memory youre training yourself that the world doesnt end when you state a preference without justifying it step 8 expect pushback and plan for it when you stop explaining your boundaries people who benefited from weak boundaries will push back hard theyll call you selfish theyll guilt trip you theyll act confused about why youre suddenly being difficult this is called an extinction burst when you stop rewarding bad behavior letting people violate your boundaries they temporarily increase that behavior to see if they can get the old response back expect it dont engage with it just keep enforcing youve changed yeah i have you used to be more flexible things are different now still not explaining still not justifying step 9 build a support system that gets it you need people in your corner who understand boundaries arent mean because when youre getting pushback from boundary violators your brain will start questioning if youre the problem find friends therapists or online communities who normalize healthy boundaries the subreddit rraisedbynarcissists is actually incredible for this even if you dont have narcissistic parents people there understand boundary enforcement in hostile environments the app finch gamifies self care and has a whole section on relationship health where you can track boundary setting as a goal and get encouragement its weirdly motivating to see your little bird celebrate when you enforce a boundary step 10 remember that boundaries protect relationships heres the counterintuitive part strong boundaries actually improve relationships the relationships that cant survive your boundaries werent healthy relationships to begin with you think youre protecting the relationship by being flexible and explaining and accommodating but youre actually building resentment youre teaching people they can push you around youre creating a dynamic where your needs dont matter boundaries are clarity they tell people how to treat you and the people who genuinely care about you will respect them without needing a thesis defense the people who get upset about your boundaries theyre upset about losing control over you let them be upset thats their work to do not yours step 11 accept that some people will choose not to respect your boundaries and then you have a different decision to make do you keep this person in your life knowing they wont respect your limits sometimes the answer is yes with modified expectations sometimes the answer is reducing contact sometimes its a full cut off but at least now youre making an informed choice instead of endlessly trying to explain yourself into respect that will never come boundaries arent about controlling other peoples behavior theyre about controlling your response to other peoples behavior you cant make someone respect your boundary but you can choose what you do when they dont

engineering and academia dont feel right looking for a more creative path hi everyone im looking for honest perspectives from people who may have gone through something similar im someone who is naturally curious creative and i enjoy learning exploring new ideas cultures and experiences i would describe myself as more alternative than traditional in terms of lifestyle and personality i like adventure creativity and environments where people are open minded and collaborative i graduated in mechanical engineering from a good university even though i never really liked the field i mostly did it because it was a safe career path family pressure and i was good at logical and technical subjects during university i also never really identified with most of my classmates naturally gravitating towards friendships with people from fields like philosophy design and geography and generally felt more comfortable in those circles after graduating i realized i didnt really connect
